title: Java News Roundup: Lazy Constants, Spring for Apache Pulsar, GlassFish, Hibernate, TomEE, Seed4J
gist: Weekly Java ecosystem roundup (Nov 9, 2026): JEP 547 Lazy Constants proposed to target JDK 28 as a fourth unchanged preview; Spring for Apache Pulsar leaves the Spring portfolio for the Apache Pulsar project; TornadoVM's jitLLM 3.0 pushes JVM-native LLM inference; plus RCs/milestones of Spring AI 2.1, Spring Boot 4.2, Hibernate ORM 8.0, GlassFish 9 and TomEE 11 converging on Jakarta Persistence 4.0.

insights.claim: JEP 547 Lazy Constants (formerly Stable Values / Computed Constants) has been proposed to target JDK 28 as a fourth preview with no changes, after three preview rounds spanning JDK 25 through JDK 27.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Repeated unchanged previews signal OpenJDK is near finalizing lazily-initialized immutable values, a JVM startup/performance primitive relevant to frameworks.

insights.claim: Lazy Constants are immutable value holders initialized at most once, offering the performance and safety benefits of final fields with flexible initialization timing.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Gives Java frameworks a standard way to defer initialization without losing JIT constant-folding, aiding startup-sensitive cloud workloads.

themes.theme: Spring ecosystem: AI APIs and governance shift

insights.claim: Spring AI 2.1.0 RC2 introduces a DecisionModel API that returns probabilities of outcomes rather than generated text, plus a VectorStoreRetriever similaritySearch method accepting user-supplied embeddings.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Enterprise Java is moving beyond chat completion toward classification-style LLM calls and bring-your-own-embedding RAG, broadening vector store usage.

insights.claim: Spring for Apache Pulsar is moving out of the Spring ecosystem to become a subproject within Apache Pulsar at the Apache Software Foundation; version 2.0.8 (October 2026) was its final Spring-branded release.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Pulsar integration ownership shifts to the Pulsar community; watch for maintenance cadence changes affecting Spring users evaluating Pulsar vs Kafka.
insights.quote: foster even deeper integration and collaboration with the broader Pulsar community.
insights.locator: The Spring for Apache Pulsar team

insights.claim: Spring Boot 4.2.0 RC2 adds X-Forwarded-Prefix support for WebFlux on Reactor Netty and fixes Redis database selection for master/replica connections.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Incremental release-candidate hardening; GA of Spring Boot 4.2 appears imminent.
insights.locator: The second release candidate of Spring Boot 4.2.0

insights.claim: Beehive Lab's TornadoVM jitLLM 3.0, a JVM-native LLM inference and serving engine, delivers 1.43x faster startup with GraalVM Native Image and up to 9.3x faster prefill, and avoids copying GGUF weights into Apple Metal buffers.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: LLM inference serving is spreading beyond Python/C++ stacks into the JVM, potentially letting Java shops serve models in-process on GPU/Metal hardware.

insights.claim: GlassFish 9.0.0-M4 and Hibernate ORM 8.0.0 CR1 both implement the Jakarta Persistence 4.0.0-M7 specification, with Hibernate also implementing Jakarta Data 1.1.0-M4 and graph-based flush coordination.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Major persistence runtimes are aligning on the next Jakarta Persistence spec, indicating a coordinated enterprise Java upgrade cycle.

insights.claim: Apache TomEE 11.0.0-M2 resolves 38 CVEs, completes Jakarta Authorization 3.0, and switches TomEE Plume to the modular EclipseLink JPA artifact.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Large CVE backlogs in app servers remain a security driver for upgrading legacy Java EE deployments.

insights.claim: Hibernate Reactive 5.1.0 and 5.0.0 release candidates align EXTENDED pessimistic lock scope with Hibernate ORM and allow adding observability via the VertxFactory interface.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Observability hooks in reactive data stacks matter for teams standardizing on OpenTelemetry-style tooling.

insights.claim: Quarkus introduced a Resiliency Testing utility that lets developers reproduce failure scenarios in @QuarkusTest application tests.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Fault-injection testing is becoming built into Java frameworks, overlapping with standalone chaos/resilience testing vendors.

insights.claim: Seed4J (formerly JHipster Lite) 2.4.0 shares one global Maven cache across its build and generated apps, and JobRunr 9.0.4 moves to hardened Docker images for build caching and security.
insights.speaker: Michael Redlich
insights.so_what: Supply-chain hardening (hardened images) is spreading into small Java OSS projects.
